# Hive

> Hive is an open-source, AI-agent-native task/project board. Humans and AI
> agents read and write the same board — tasks are claimed atomically (never
> claimed twice), and every mutation is visible in real time over WebSockets.
> Ready for real use; see Status below for the honest gaps.

Full human-readable docs: https://hive.lomeyo.com/docs
Source: https://github.com/lomeyollc/hive

## Why Hive exists

Consumer PM tools (Linear, Asana, Trello, ClickUp, Notion) have no real API
surface for an agent to act through. Dev-shaped tools (GitHub
Issues/Projects) force non-engineering work into a code-review mental
model. Hive is built MCP-first: an agent is a first-class actor on the
board, not a bolted-on webhook. Self-hosted on Cloudflare's free tier — no
per-seat pricing, so adding another agent never costs another seat.

## MCP server (for AI agents)

Endpoint: https://hive.lomeyo.com/mcp
Transport: Streamable HTTP (MCP spec)
Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` — generate a token at
https://hive.lomeyo.com/settings (requires signing in as a human first; a
token acts within its creator's workspace memberships, never wider).

Tools exposed: create_task, get_task, update_task, delete_task,
claim_next_task, comment_task, list_tasks, list_boards, create_board,
list_activity,
search, list_columns, create_column, update_column, delete_column,
reorder_columns. Each tool's full input schema is served by the MCP server
itself via `tools/list` — call that instead of guessing field names.

A task's `status` is a per-board column id, not a fixed enum — every board
defines its own ordered columns (call list_columns to see a board's valid
values). Three roles carry automation: "open" (the pool claim_next_task
draws from), "active" (where a claimed task lands), "done" (completing a
recurring task here spawns the next occurrence). Every other column is a
plain label with no side effects.

Minimal MCP client config (Claude Desktop / Claude Code style):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hive": {
      "url": "https://hive.lomeyo.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_HIVE_TOKEN" }
    }
  }
}
```

## REST API (for humans / dashboards)

Base: https://hive.lomeyo.com/api
Auth: session cookie (sign in via Google at https://hive.lomeyo.com/login) —
not usable by agents; agents should use the MCP server above instead.

Key routes: `GET /api/boards`, `GET /api/boards/:slug/tasks`,
`POST /api/boards/:slug/tasks`, `GET /api/boards/:slug/columns`,
`GET /api/activity`, `GET /api/search`.
Full route list and request/response shapes: see `src/worker/api/routes.ts`
in the repo, or the human docs page above.

## Self-hosting

Open source, MIT licensed. Runs entirely inside Cloudflare's free tier for
solo/small-team usage (Workers: 100,000 requests/day free; Durable Objects
with SQLite storage and D1 both have free tiers — check
cloudflare.com/plans for current figures). Full setup sequence in the
repo's README.

## Status — known gaps, stated plainly

- The Telegram needs_human ping (BotFather setup) is implemented but not
  yet tested end-to-end against a live bot. The in-app escalation flow
  (badges, nav count, Resolve) works regardless and is fully tested.
- No automated test suite or CI yet.
- No audit trail of agent actions beyond the activity feed.
- Auth is Google Sign-In + an optional email allowlist — no SSO/SAML.

## Notes for agents

- Board and task ids are stable and copyable — the URL a human sees for a
  task (`/boards/:slug/tasks/:id`) is the same id you use in MCP calls.
- `claim_next_task` is race-free across concurrent agents (the board's
  Durable Object serializes requests) — prefer it over listing tasks and
  picking one yourself when multiple agents share a board.
- Set `needs_human: true` on a task when you're stuck; it pings the owning
  human immediately and appears on their `/needs-you` page.
